identity.title: The MESAS Project: Long-wavelength Follow-up Observations of Sirius A

paper_type_evidence.quote: Here we present ALMA, GBT, and VLA observations of Sirius A, the closest main-sequence A-type star, that span from 1.4 to 9.0 millimeters.

evidence.quote: The observations were centered on Sirius A using J2000 coordinates RA = 06 h 45 m 08.30 s and $\delta = -16^{\circ} ~43' ~18.91''$.

question.value: What is the long-wavelength (1.4-9 mm) emission of Sirius A, and is it consistent with PHOENIX stellar atmosphere models and stable over time?

evidence.quote: These observations complement our previous millimeter data on Sirius A and are entirely consistent with the PHOENIX stellar atmosphere models constructed to explain them.
We observed Sirius A with the *Atacama Large Millimeter Array* (ALMA) during Cycle 5 (ID 2017.1.00698.S, PI White).
The observations in ALMA Bands 3, 4, and 5 were taken in 3 separate executions blocks (EBs) from January through August.

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: 4 SPWs per band, 128x15.625 MHz channels each; Band 5 centered 196/198/208/210 GHz; Band 4 143/145/155/157 GHz; Band 3 93/95/105/107 GHz

evidence.quote: Each SPW has $128\times 15.625$ MHz channels for a total bandwidth of 2 GHz.
The SPWs were centered at 93 GHz, 95 GHz, 105 GHz, and 107 GHz, giving an effective continuum frequency of 100 GHz (3.0 mm).
Each band utilized an instrument configuration with a total bandwidth of 8 GHz split among 4 spectral windows (SPW).
This EB used a 43 antenna configuration with baselines ranging from 15 m to 1397 m.
The size of the resulting synthesized beam is $1.02''\times0.69''$ at a position angle of $68.2^{\circ}$, corresponding to $\sim2.3$ au.
These Band 4 data achieve a RMS sensitivity of $0.029~\rm mJy~beam^{-1}$ in the CLEANed image.
The Band 5 observations were made on 2018 August 22 for 20.24 min (5.1 min on-source).
The Band 3 observations were made on 2018 January 25 for 19.75 min (5.12 min on-source).
during Cycle 5 (ID 2017.1.00698.S, PI White)
The data from the VLA were acquired in Semester 18A on 2018 September 07 and 2018 September 11 (ID 18A-328, PI White).
The total on-source time was 104 min split roughly equally between nights.

evidence.quote: All of the data were reduced using the Common Astronomy Software Applications (CASA 5.4.0) pipeline (cite: casa_reference)
Data were reduced using the CASA 5.4.0 pipeline
The flux and bandpass were calibrated with quasar J0750+1231, the phase with J0648-1744
For ALMA, we adopt an absolute flux calibration uncertainty of $10\%$ and for VLA $20\%$
The data were imaged with a natural weighting and cleaned using CASA’s *CLEAN* algorithm down to a threshold of 1/2 the RMS noise.
The 2018 September 11 observations achieve sensitivities of $0.028~\rm mJy~beam^{-1}$ and $0.014~\rm mJy~beam^{-1}$, respectively.

evidence.quote: The Scheduling Block (SB) for each observation was setup identically to the previous VLA observations of Sirius A (cite: white18)
As in (cite: white18), we use the CASA task *uvmodelfit* to obtain a flux at each wavelength.

analysis_steps.goal: Fit point-source fluxes to ALMA and VLA visibilities

method.value: Point-source fit to visibilities per SPW with minimum chi-squared iteration

evidence.quote: This approach fits a point source to the visibilities of a given data set. A minimum $\chi^{2}$ is converged on through an iterative procedure.

assumptions.value: Sirius A is a point source (0.00602")

evidence.quote: Sirius A is effectively a point source ($0.00602''$)

method.value: Map of all GBT data, Gaussian fit at Sirius A position

evidence.quote: we generated a map of all the GBT data and fit a Gaussian at the location of Sirius A.

validation.value: Fake sources injected into timestreams and recovered

evidence.quote: fake sources of known amplitude were added to the raw timestreams and were recovered with high accuracy.

method.value: Non-linear least squares fit of T_obs = C0 T_phot (lambda/0.45mm)^alpha over 0.45-9.0 mm

evidence.quote: Using a non-linear least squares model fitting procedure with the Python SciPy function *curve_fit*, we find best fit values of C$_{0} = 0.67\pm 0.03$ and $\alpha = 0.05\pm 0.02$.

assumptions.value: Rayleigh-Jeans limit, T_obs substituted for T_B

evidence.quote: by assuming the stellar emission is in the Rayleigh-Jeans limit and substituting $T_{obs}$ for T$_{B}$
Using a non-linear least squares model fitting procedure with the Python SciPy function *curve_fit*, we find best fit values of C$_{0} = 0.67\pm 0.03$ and $\alpha = 0.05\pm 0.02$.
